title: QBR Framework: Health Packs & Renewal Checklist (Standard + Enterprise)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working QBR slide and facilitator notes pack intended to be a fast-start template for Customer Success Managers (CSMs). It contains two parallel slide flows (Standard customer and Enterprise customer) plus an operational renewal checklist and an at-risk playbook. Use this as a starting point — replace placeholders, inject account metrics, and sync with Sales/AE before presenting.

Audience:
- CSMs leading QBRs (primary)
- AEs and Solutions Engineers (secondary)
- Customer execs and technical leads (presentation recipients)

How to use:
- Pick the flow that matches the account tier (Standard vs Enterprise).
- Populate the front page with up-to-date adoption metrics and one-line executive summary.
- Save a copy per account: QBR-<customer>-YYYY-MM-DD.
- Link any open Jira/Confluence items for technical follow-ups in the appendix.

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE (high level):
1) Title + Executive one-liner (1 slide)
2) Health Snapshot (1 slide)
3) Usage & Adoption (2 slides)
4) Success against goals (1–2 slides)
5) Risks & Dependencies (1 slide)
6) Roadmap & Opportunities (1 slide)
7) Renewal & Next Steps (1 slide)
8) Appendix: technical items, open action tracker, renewal checklist (several slides)

Standard flow (recommended for SMB / mid-market):
Slide 1 — Title + Exec Summary (2 min)
- Slide elements: logo, meeting date, CSM/AE names, 1-sentence outcome ("On track for renew, growth opportunity: embedding model X in product Y").
- Speaker note: State meeting objective and expected decisions (e.g., review health, confirm renewal intent, align on next steps).

Slide 2 — Health Snapshot (3 min)
- Metrics to include: health score (0–100), usage trend (30/60/90 days), NPS (if available), open critical incidents last 90 days.
- Placeholder: "Health score = 40% usage + 40% error-rate-adjusted uptime + 20% engagement" (customize per account).

Slide 3 — Usage & Feature Adoption (5 min)
- Bullet areas: Top APIs used, peak QPS, average latency, percent of traffic on cached paths, embedding calls vs generation calls.
- Quick wins: suggested optimizations (batching, caching prefixes) with estimated cost impact.

Slide 4 — Outcomes vs Goals (5 min)
- Show 2–3 customer goals from kickoff/contract and quantitative progress (e.g., time to result down 40%).
- Testimonials / customer quotes if available.

Slide 5 — Risks & Actions (3 min)
- One-line risk, impact, owner, mitigation. Keep ledger short (top 3).

Slide 6 — Renewal & Ask (2 min)
- Renewal date, current ARR, suggested motion (standard renewal / upsell / expansion), next meeting.

Enterprise flow (expanded — recommended for enterprise strategic accounts):
Slide 1 — Title + Strategic Exec Summary (2 min)
- Condense account health and the single ask to the exec sponsor.

Slide 2 — Business Impact & ROI (5 min)
- Map Redwood platform metrics to customer business KPIs: cost per inference, latency SLAs, conversion or revenue tied to response time.
- Include an ROI table (baseline vs with optimizations).

Slide 3 — Adoption & Architecture Review (5–7 min)
- Technical diagram (where Redwood sits in infra).
- Versioning/variant usage and pinned models, security posture (VPC/private deployment), data residency notes.

Slide 4 — Operations & Reliability (4 min)
- Incident summary, MTTR, recent rollouts, canary success metrics.

Slide 5 — Strategic Roadmap Alignment (4 min)
- Opportunities for co-innovation, pilot ideas (private deployment, dedicated capacity), timelines.

Slide 6 — Commercial Positioning & Renewal Options (4 min)
- Present 3 options: renew-as-is, renew + modest expansion, enterprise commitment with Dedicated/Private.
- Highlight SLAs and entitlements for enterprise contract.

Slide 7 — Action Plan & Commitment (3 min)
- Clear asks and owners, legal/commercial next steps, timeline to final proposal.

Appendix (both flows):
- Technical action tracker (link to Confluence/Jira items)
- Detailed metric definitions and data sources
- Past QBR archive (last 4 quarters)

Renewal Checklist (operational, copy this into customer binder):
- Renewal owner assigned (Name, AE/CS)
- Renewal window open date (T-minus 90 days)
- Current contract end date (date)
- Last committed ARR and add-on usage report attached
- Health score trend: last 90 / 180 / 365 days
- Open technical blockers impacting renewal (list)
- Escalation path: SE on-call, solutions lead, customer exec sponsor
- Draft commercial options prepared (baseline, expansion, enterprise)
- Legal/compliance review required? (Yes/No)
- Internal approval due (sales ops, finance) and dates

Sample Renewal Tracker (columns to copy into a sheet):
- Customer Name | CSM | AE | Renewal Date | Contract ARR | Expansion Upside | Health Score | Top Risk | Renewal Status | Next Contact Date | Notes | Jira/Confluence Links
- Use conditional coloring: Health Score <50 => At-risk, Renewal Status in {At-risk, On-track, Upsell}.

At-risk playbook (quick triage):
1) Immediate: raise flag in weekly CS sync + create dedicated Slack channel with AE/SE (owner: CSM).
2) 48 hours: run operational readiness checklist (latency/cost spikes, auth failures, model regressions).
3) 72 hours: schedule technical deep dive with SE + customer engineering; produce remediation plan.
4) 7 days: schedule exec-to-exec alignment if remediation plan still outstanding.
5) Ongoing: weekly touchpoint until risk reduced, track closure in tracker.

Suggested KPIs & Measurement notes (source recommended):
- Active endpoints: count over 30/60/90 days (from usage logs).
- Token volume and cost per 1k tokens (billing + estimated infra overhead).
- Latency p95 and p99 (split by model/route).
- Error rate (% failed requests) and incident rollups.
- Cache hit ratio (application + KV prefix cache).

Speaker prompts (short scripts):
- Opening: "Thanks for joining — we want to spend 20 minutes reviewing outcomes and 10 minutes planning next steps. Our objective is to confirm the renewal path and identify any blockers we should clear together"
- If customer disengaged: "We noticed usage drift in the last 60 days — helpful to understand whether priorities changed or there are blockers we can resolve."
- If at-risk: "We’ve escalated to our solutions team and have a remediation plan; we’d like your buy-in on proposed timeline so we can eliminate the risk before renewal."

Email follow-up templates (short):
- Post-QBR summary (subject): "QBR recap & next steps — <Customer>"
- Body: 3 bullets: 1) outcome/renewal posture, 2) top 3 actions + owners + dates, 3) link to updated tracker and next meeting.

TODOs / Open questions (CS internal):

- [ ] Link automated usage dashboard in slide deck (Diego to confirm data source).
- [ ] Define SLA language for Dedicated trial offers (legal review pending).

Notes / context snippets for presenter:
- Keep slides visually light: charts for trends, 3–5 bullets per slide.
- Executive audience wants outcomes and asks first — move detailed architecture to appendix.
- Emphasize predictable economics: show how batching/caching recommendations reduce unit cost.

Change log (working notes):

- 2024-10-28: Added enterprise ROI slide and sample tracker (Priya)

References & links: (placeholders — replace with account-specific links)
- Confluence: QBR Framework home (linked above)
- Jira board: CS-2145 (renewal pipeline)
- GitHub: PR with slide templates (linked above)

Quick formatting checklist before sending to customer:
- Remove internal Slack links and Jira comments
- Replace sample numbers with actual account metrics
- Confirm attendee list and tailor executive one-liner

End of document — this is a working draft. Use feedback to iterate; keep the copy-per-customer model to maintain auditability.
